I'm a Muslim, so I guess I should think about this from an Islamic perspective. First, I remember that in Islam, there are teachings about treating others with kindness and not seeking harm. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized treating people well, even enemies. So, if a woman is wishing harm on her ex, that might go against those teachings. But wait, maybe she's feeling hurt or upset because of the breakup. It's possible she's acting out of emotional pain. But Islam also teaches that we should control our emotions and not let them lead us to do wrong things. So, even if she's hurt, wishing someone harm isn't the right approach. I also think about the concept of forgiveness in Islam. The Quran says, "Let not a people's ill deed cause you to despair of God's mercy." So, maybe she should focus on forgiving him and moving on rather than holding onto anger. Another point is the idea of not seeking revenge. The Prophet said, "No one wrongs a person and then that person forgives them except that God increases their reward." So, seeking revenge, even through words, isn't encouraged. I wonder if there's a difference between wishing harm and actually causing harm. But in Islam, intentions matter a lot. Wishing someone harm is still a negative intention, even if it doesn't result in action. So, it's still not right. Also, considering the consequences, if she tells him that, it might cause more pain or escalate the situation. It's better to handle things with maturity and grace, as Islam advises. In summary, from what I understand, wishing someone harm, even if they've wronged you, isn't in line with Islamic teachings. It's better to seek forgiveness, control emotions, and treat others kindly.
